steps.title: Gather materials and equipment
steps.instruction: Collect all required items: UV‑C light source (254 nm) calibrated with a VLX‑3W radiometer, UV‑protective eyewear and safety shielding, UV safety shielding, XP‑V (XP30RO) fibroblasts (POLH−/−) and XP‑V Comp (XP30RO complemented) fibroblasts, fibroblast culture medium (DMEM High‑Glucose + 10 % FBS + 1 % antibiotic/antimycotic), SYBR Green I nucleic acid gel stain (10 000× concentrate in DMSO; Life Technologies, cat. no. S11494), 1× PBS, sterile amber micro‑centrifuge tubes (or clear tubes wrapped in foil), pipettes, and a light‑protected storage container.

steps.title: Prepare SYBR Green I staining solution
steps.instruction: In a sterile amber micro‑centrifuge tube (or a clear tube wrapped in foil), add 9 999 µL of freshly prepared or pre‑chilled 1× PBS, then add 1 µL of SYBR Green I (10 000× stock) to obtain a 1:10 000 dilution (final volume 10 000 µL, 1×). Mix gently by pipetting up and down; do not vortex. Protect the solution from light at all times. If not used immediately, store the solution in a light‑protected container at room temperature for up to 6 months.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 µL SYBR Green I (10 000× stock).
Mix gently by pipetting up and down.
Keep protected from light; store up to 6 months if needed.

steps.title: Run alkaline BrdU comet assay (basic protocol with XP‑V modifications)
steps.instruction: Follow the standard alkaline BrdU comet assay steps as described in the Basic Protocol, applying the following modifications: use XP‑V (POLH−/−) and XP‑V Comp fibroblasts cultured in DMEM High‑Glucose + 10 % FBS + 1 % antibiotic/antimycotic; expose cells to UV‑C light (254 nm) calibrated with the VLX‑3W radiometer as required; employ UV‑protective eyewear and shielding throughout irradiation; and incorporate any other XP‑V‑specific adjustments noted in the Basic Protocol.

substeps.instruction: Culture XP‑V and XP‑V Comp fibroblasts in the specified medium.
Expose cells to calibrated UV‑C (254 nm) using appropriate safety shielding.
Proceed with the remaining steps of the Basic Protocol (cell embedding in agarose, lysis, alkaline unwinding, electrophoresis, neutralization, etc.).

steps.title: Image comets and select analysis channels
steps.instruction: Capture fluorescence images of the comets, selecting the appropriate comet type and fluorescence channel for each measurement: use the BrdU channel to quantify replication‑associated DNA damage and the SYBR Green channel to assess total genomic DNA damage. Ensure consistent exposure settings across samples.

substeps.instruction: Acquire images in the BrdU fluorescence channel.
Acquire images in the SYBR Green fluorescence channel (or both channels together).
Verify that comet type (e.g., tail length, intensity) is appropriate for the analysis.

steps.title: Compile data and generate graphs
steps.instruction: Quantify Olive Tail Moment (or other comet parameters) for each nucleoids, then calculate mean ± standard deviation (SD) for technical and biological replicates. Use GraphPad Prism (or equivalent) to create bar graphs (mean ± SD) or scatter plots (individual data points). Pre‑define statistical significance threshold (e.g., p < 0.05).

substeps.instruction: Calculate mean, median, and SD for each condition.
Create bar graphs showing mean ± SD for BrdU‑only and BrdU + SYBR data.
Create scatter plots displaying at least 200 nucleoids per treatment from ≥ 2 independent experiments.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Use an Excel template or similar to compute descriptive statistics. For comparisons between two groups, apply an unpaired Student’s t‑test; for three or more groups, perform one‑way ANOVA followed by Bonferroni’s (or Tukey’s HSD) post‑hoc test. Verify normality assumptions; if violated, use non‑parametric tests such as Mann‑Whitney U or Kruskal‑Wallis. Follow MIRCA guidelines when reporting comet assay data.

substeps.instruction: Create Excel sheet with raw Olive Tail Moment values.
Run appropriate statistical test (t‑test, ANOVA, etc.).
Check normality; switch to non‑parametric tests if needed.
Document statistical methods according to MIRCA recommendations.
